question:
I have a dbt project that has a single profile with two targets in my profiles.yml:

my_project:
  target: target_a
  outputs:
    target_a: 
      ...
    target_b: 
      ...

I have a file structure that looks like:

int/
  folder_a/
    _models__folder_a.yml
    int_a_sql_job.sql
    int_a_sql_job2.sql
  folder_b/
    _models__folder_b.yml
    int_b_sql_job.sql

target_a is the default target and is used for folder_a jobs, which is what I want. However, for all jobs in folder_b I need to use the target_b target. Passing --target target_b in the command line works, but I need this to be overridden from within the codebase itself, specifically in the _models__folder_b. How do I do that?

EDIT:

The reason I need this: I want all jobs in folder_b to write to a different schema, but that schema needs to be dynamic. When I'm running this on my staging server, folder_a needs to write to folder_a_staging_schema and folder_b needs to write to folder_b_staging_schema. When I'm running this on my prod server, folder_a needs to write to folder_a_schema and folder_b needs to write to folder_b_schema.

I'm realizing now that dbt probably cannot do this, cause dbt uses one single target for the entire duration of running a single command.

I'm open to other ideas, but I want to be able to dbt run and everything builds to the correct schema (i.e. not running jobs separately with the --target flag)
title: Use DBT Targets Dynamically
answer:
why dont you just add a different schema for each folder? like

---staging (for all other folders)
     |---staging A (folder A)
     |---staging B (folder B)

and in the dbt_project.yml

staging:
    +schema: staging
    folder_a:
        +schema: staging_folder_a
    folder_b:
        +schema: staging_folder_b
